Job Description:

The AVP, Strategic Programs, Innovation, Insights & Regulatory Operations provides executive leadership across Strategic Initiatives & Innovation, Data & Insights, Registration & Licensing, and Governance Programs & Initiatives. The role integrates regulatory execution, governance and control frameworks, modernization, portfolio delivery and business priorities through a common strategy, roadmap and operating model.

The AVP sets priorities, allocates resources, leads the Director team, and ensures initiatives move from concept through adoption and sustainable ownership. The role balances regulatory defensibility, operational risk, advisor and client experience, efficiency, capacity and responsible use of digital, automation, analytics, AI and emerging technologies.

What will you do?

Strong knowledge of Canadian wealth and insurance distribution, securities and insurance regulatory requirements, dealer obligations and first-line supervisory expectations.
Experience operating in a federally regulated financial institution, ideally within an OSFI-regulated environment and across a three-lines-of-defence model.
Demonstrated success leading leaders and multidisciplinary teams through complex operational, regulatory and organizational change.
Proven ability to translate regulatory change, audit findings, control gaps and business risks into practical operating-model, process, technology and governance solutions.
Advanced portfolio-management capability, including prioritization, governance, benefits realization, resource planning and executive reporting.
Exceptional judgment, strategic thinking, stakeholder influence, executive communication and ability to challenge constructively in a complex matrixed organization.

What do you need to succeed?

Significant progressive leadership experience (10 years+) in financial services, ideally spanning wealth, insurance, governance, regulatory operations, compliance, risk, transformation or technology-enabled change.

Strategy, Portfolio, Executive Partnership and Change Leadership

Set and execute an integrated multi-year strategy and roadmap aligned to BG&C and RA&S priorities, regulatory obligations, business outcomes and investment capacity.
Establish disciplined portfolio governance for intake, prioritization, sequencing, benefits realization, executive reporting and transition to business ownership.
Advise senior leaders on outcomes, trade-offs, dependencies, risks, capability gaps and required decisions or escalations.
Build enterprise partnerships and lead portfolio-level change through clear direction, stakeholder engagement, communication, training, adoption and accountability.

Governance, Regulatory Execution and First-Line Oversight

Strengthen regulatory defensibility and first-line ownership by embedding practical governance, control and supervision capabilities across the portfolio.
Establish, embed and maintain governance and control frameworks that support regulatory compliance, effective first-line oversight, advisor/client outcomes and sustainable business ownership.
Lead applicable regulatory change execution from horizon scanning and impact assessment through business requirements, implementation, adoption and evidence of sustainable compliance.
Oversee attestations, audit/regulatory findings, remediation commitments and management action plans to ensure timely, complete and sustainable closure.
Ensure field leaders, advisors and business partners receive clear guidance, communications and training to support adoption of applicable governance, regulatory and operational expectations.

Transformation, Innovation, Insights and Regulatory Operations

Develop and execute the modernization roadmap across process and operating-model redesign, technology, analytics, automation, AI and GenAI-enabled capabilities.
Provide executive oversight of registration and licensing operations, ensuring clear accountability, documented decisions, effective controls and alignment with regulatory and business requirements.
Set direction for analytics, dashboards and performance measures that connect regulatory risk, advisor and client experience and business outcomes.
Sponsor discovery through scaling, using evidence-based criteria to stop, iterate or expand solutions while ensuring adoption, controls and sustainable ownership.

jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Territory Design & Maintenance

Leading territory design and account segmentation, aligning selling resources with company strategy.
Translating revenue targets into coverage models and account assignments, and identifying where the organization is over- or under-covered and what needs to change.
Owning ongoing territory maintenance, including account assignments and in-year territory changes.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Identify practical opportunities to improve budgeting, forecasting, reporting and analytics capabilities.

Support knowledge transfer, coaching and capability-building within the finance team.
Leave behind a clear transition plan and roadmap for continued improvement beyond the assignment.

Standardized and more efficient finance processes and workflows.
Enhanced utilization of financial systems, reporting tools and analytics capabilities.

Financial leadership & strategy

Own company-wide financial planning, forecasting, and performance tracking, including SaaS metrics and operating models

Use Agentic AI to automate key processes such as: accounts receivable, month-end close, and financial package preparation

Lead and mentor the finance and accounting team, setting a high bar for accountability and performance
Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration

Familiarity with BI or dashboarding tools (e.g., Metabase, Looker, Tableau)
Experience supporting board reporting and investor relations

jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Territory Design & Maintenance

Leading territory design and account segmentation, aligning selling resources with company strategy.
Translating revenue targets into coverage models and account assignments, and identifying where the organization is over- or under-covered and what needs to change.
Owning ongoing territory maintenance, including account assignments and in-year territory changes.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. Accountable to and funded by the over 15,000 pulse growers in the province, we provide leadership and work to create opportunities for profitable growth of the Saskatchewan pulses by investing in research, market development, communications, and agronomy extension. At SPG, we see diversity as an asset and strive to make our work and our organization inclusive. We are committed to ensuring equal opportunities and an inclusive environment where everyone feels they can bring their whole self to work.

Director of Finance and Operations

SPG is seeking a strategic and collaborative Director of Finance and Operations
to provide leadership across the organization’s financial management and operational functions.

As a member of the Leadership Team, the Director will oversee budgeting, financial reporting, audit coordination, financial compliance, and business analysis. The role is also responsible for key corporate operations, including office management, information technology, payroll, employee benefits, insurance, and facilities.

This is an opportunity for an experienced or developing finance leader who can balance strong financial stewardship with practical operational decision-making. The successful candidate will report to the Executive Director, and work closely with the Leadership Team, Board of Directors, and the Audit and Finance Committee while leading and supporting a small finance and administrative team.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Financial Leadership

Lead budgeting, financial reporting, and external audit processes.
Prepare quarterly financial statements and variance analyses.
Develop financial policies and ensure compliance with legislation, organizational policies, and funding agreements.
Provide financial analysis and support strategic planning and decision-making.

Operations

Oversee corporate operations, including information technology, payroll, benefits, insurance, facilities, and office administration.
Support governance policy reviews and serve as SPG’s Privacy Officer.
Promote effective stewardship of organizational resources.

Lead and Develop the Team

Provide leadership and direction to the finance and administrative team.
Develop and monitor departmental plans and budgets.
Set clear expectations, delegate effectively, and support employee development.
Foster a collaborative, accountable, and respectful workplace.
Oversee performance management and routine supervisory responsibilities.

Contribute to Organizational Leadership

Participate as an active member of the Leadership Team.
Provide advice on organizational strategy, governance, and policy matters.
Support the consistent application of organizational policies.
Lead or contribute to special projects and prepare Board reports and presentations as required.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting, finance, or a related field.
A professional accounting (CPA) or finance designation.
Minimum three years of experience in a finance leadership role.

IMMEDIATE INTERIM OPPORTUNITY

Interim Vice President, Finance & Transformation

Reports To: Chief Executive Officer

Duration: 12 months

Location: Downtown Toronto

(Hybrid)

This is an exceptional opportunity to lead a high-impact transformation mandate within a well-known, mission-driven organization undertaking a significant modernization journey. Few interim mandates offer the opportunity to influence both organizational transformation and finance modernization at this scale. Our client is embarking on an ambitious journey to strengthen its capabilities, modernize core operations, and position itself for long-term success.

As the Interim, you will be at the center of that journey. Working directly with the CEO and senior leadership team, you will assess the effectiveness of the finance organization, redesign key processes and structures, oversee the implementation of a modern accounting platform, strengthen governance and reporting capabilities, and help create a high-performing finance function that delivers meaningful insight and strategic value. This is an opportunity to make a visible impact, build lasting capability, and leave behind a stronger, more modern organization than the one you inherited.

Key Priorities

1. Assess and Shape the Finance Transformation Roadmap

Conduct a focused current-state assessment of finance processes, controls, reporting, governance and supporting capabilities.
Identify gaps, risks, inefficiencies and opportunities to strengthen the maturity and effectiveness of the finance function.
Develop and sequence a practical transformation roadmap with clear priorities, accountabilities and measurable outcomes.

2. Strengthen Financial Planning, Reporting and Decision Support

Review budgeting, forecasting, financial planning and management reporting practices.
Improve the quality, consistency and usefulness of financial information available to executives, the Finance & Audit Committee and the Board.
Help translate financial information into clear implications, options and recommendations for decision-making.

3. Enhance Governance, Controls and Risk Management

Strengthen financial policies, internal controls, documentation and oversight practices.
Support the identification, assessment and management of financial risks.
Provide guidance related to internal and external audit readiness and follow-through.

4. Drive Process Improvement and Operational Excellence

Review workflows to identify bottlenecks, manual workarounds, duplication and control gaps.
Standardize and simplify processes to improve accuracy, efficiency, accountability and service delivery.
Promote effective collaboration between finance and organizational stakeholders.

5. Enable Technology and Reporting Modernization

Assess how existing financial systems and reporting tools are being used.
Identify practical opportunities to improve budgeting, forecasting, reporting and analytics capabilities.
Reduce unnecessary reliance on manual processes and spreadsheets where feasible.

6. Build Sustainable Capability

Create practical tools, templates, policies, procedures and standard operating practices.
Support knowledge transfer, coaching and capability-building within the finance team.
Leave behind a clear transition plan and roadmap for continued improvement beyond the assignment.

Expected Deliverables

A validated current-state assessment and prioritized finance transformation roadmap.
Strengthened budgeting, forecasting, reporting and decision-support practices.
Improved financial policies, controls, governance documentation and risk oversight.
Standardized and more efficient finance processes and workflows.
Enhanced utilization of financial systems, reporting tools and analytics capabilities.
Practical implementation support, knowledge transfer and a sustainable transition plan.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be a seasoned finance transformation leader who combines strategic judgment with a practical, implementation-oriented approach. They will be comfortable advising senior leaders and governance stakeholders while working directly with teams to translate recommendations into durable improvements.

University degree in finance, accounting, business administration or a related discipline.
Professional accounting designation in good standing is strongly preferred.
10+ years of progressively senior finance and leadership experience, including executive or senior management exposure.
Demonstrated experience leading finance transformation, strengthening controls and improving management reporting.
Experience supporting a Board, Finance & Audit Committee or an equivalent governance body.
Strong process improvement, change management, project leadership and implementation capability.
Ability to provide clear, practical and candid advice and to translate financial information for varied stakeholders.
Experience in a regulatory, public-sector, healthcare, not-for-profit or other public-interest organization is considered an asset.
High integrity, discretion, accountability and commitment to public-interest stewardship.

Read about our mission, story and values here.

To find out more about our perks, click here.

Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here.

Thriving At Rewind

We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:

Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.
Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.
Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.
Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.
Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

About The Role

We’re looking for a senior finance leader to own and evolve Rewind’s full finance function spanning accounting, financial planning, and controller responsibilities. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution: you’ll bring a strong accounting foundation, step confidently into hands-on operational work when needed, and guide the business with clear, data-driven insight.

This is a hands on builder role. You’ll shape the broader finance strategy, while also performing core Accounting and Controller responsibilities. You should expect to roll up your sleeves and operate as both a leader and an individual contributor, handling everything from Board reporting, to financial modelling, to processing payroll and driving month end close. You’ll partner closely with the executive team, particularly the CEO and CRO to ensure Rewind scales with financial clarity, discipline, and confidence.

Financial leadership & strategy

Own company-wide financial planning, forecasting, and performance tracking, including SaaS metrics and operating models
Partner with leadership to guide investment decisions, pricing strategy, and growth planning
Deliver clear, actionable financial insights to executives, board members, and investors
Support strategic finance work including scenario planning and executive-level analysis.

Accounting, close operations & compliance

Oversee and continuously improve the month-end close process, ensuring accurate and timely reporting across P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow
Maintain high-quality financial reporting and variance analysis to support decision-making
Step into hands-on accounting work where needed, ensuring no gaps in execution as the team scales
Own all core accounting operations, including AP/AR, payroll, treasury, and general ledger management
Lead audits, tax filings, and compliance across jurisdictions, including SR&ED and international subsidiaries
Manage equity administration (e.g., Carta), ensuring accurate cap table and regulatory compliance

Controls, governance & infrastructure

Strengthen internal controls and financial processes to safeguard company assets and support scale
Oversee vendor relationships, banking, insurance programs, and external partners (auditors, consultants)
Build and evolve systems, tooling, and workflows to improve accuracy, efficiency, and visibility
Oversee the stock option/equity program and management of the cap table.

Leverage Agentic AI

Use Agentic AI to automate key processes such as: accounts receivable, month-end close, and financial package preparation

Team leadership & development

Lead and mentor the finance and accounting team, setting a high bar for accountability and performance
Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, and cross-functional collaboration

What You’ll Bring

Experience in a venture-backed or scaling SaaS company
CPA designation (or equivalent) with 10+ years of progressive experience across accounting and finance
Early-career foundation in accounting (e.g., audit, controllership) with a transition into broader finance leadership
Experience owning both accounting operations and FP&A in a high-growth SaaS or tech environment
Strong understanding of SaaS metrics, revenue recognition, and financial best practices
Proficiency using AI tools to streamline and enhance financial modelling, reporting and workflows
Comfort operating as a hands-on leader, including stepping into payroll, reporting, or operational tasks when needed
Proven ability to build, improve, and scale financial processes and systems
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex financial data into clear insights
Experience with modern finance tools (e.g., NetSuite, Salesforce, Stripe, Carta, QuickBooks Online)

Nice to have

Exposure to international finance operations and multi-entity structures
Experience managing or implementing financial systems and automation initiatives
Familiarity with BI or dashboarding tools (e.g., Metabase, Looker, Tableau)
Experience supporting board reporting and investor relations

Location

There is a strong preference for candidates based in Ontario for easier collaboration and occasional in-person meetings in our HQ office (Ottawa).

Compensation Philosophy

The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process.

In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.

If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.

Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.

Why join Rewind

At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.

We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.

How Rewind Will Support You

We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to:

Flexible work hours
Employee stock options
Health benefits
3 weeks vacation
7 life leave days
2 Level Up days for professional development
1 volunteer day
Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December
Paid parental leave
$2000/year wellness/home office allowance

Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We value how each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective, and we are always eager to further diversify our company. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.

new_jobs.description:
Clio is the global leader in legal AI technology, empowering legal professionals and law firms of every size to work smarter, faster, and more securely.

We are transforming the legal experience for all by bettering the lives of legal professionals while increasing access to justice.

Summary:

Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation
to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US.

This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

What you’ll work on:

GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas

Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

Territory Design & Maintenance

Leading territory design and account segmentation, aligning selling resources with company strategy.
Translating revenue targets into coverage models and account assignments, and identifying where the organization is over- or under-covered and what needs to change.
Owning ongoing territory maintenance, including account assignments and in-year territory changes.

Compensation Strategy & Plan Design

Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

Compensation Administration & Systems

Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership & Team Development

Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

What you bring:

8+ years of experience in SaaS or technology, with direct ownership of capacity planning, territory, quota, and compensation design.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a strategic advisor to senior GTM and Finance leaders.
Excellent executive-level communication skills, both written and verbal.
Experience leading and developing teams, with a focus on coaching and accountability.
High integrity, sound judgment, and comfort handling sensitive information.
Ability to thrive in ambiguity, make high-quality decisions with incomplete data, and drive outcomes in a fast-paced environment.
Action oriented, ownership driven mindset with a strong bias toward impact and results.
Proven ability to develop presentations with strong visual storytelling.
Advanced Excel skills.
Experience in translating measurements into recommendations, and connecting multiple data sources and building dashboards in data visualization tools (CRMA, Looker, Tableau, Google Sheets).
Knowledge of statistical modeling techniques.
Fluency in Salesforce data and at least one planning or ICM platform.

What you will find here:

Compensation is one of the main components of Clio’s Total Rewards Program. We have developed a series of programs and processes to ensure we are creating fair and competitive pay practices that form the foundation of our human and high-performing culture.

Some highlights of our Total Rewards program include:

Competitive, equitable salary with top-tier health benefits, dental, and vision insurance
Hybrid work environment, with expectation for local Clions (Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Dublin and Sydney) to be in office minimum twice per week.
Flexible time off policy, with an encouraged 20 days off per year.
EAP benefits for you and household members, including counseling and online resources
401k matching and Child Education Savings
Clioversary recognition program with special acknowledgement at 3, 5, 7, and 10 years

The on-target earnings (OTE) salary range for this role is $207,400 to $311,000 reflecting base salary plus variable compensation at 100% attainment. Variable compensation is not guaranteed and will depend on individual, team, or company performance. Initial placement within the range is informed by geographic region, experience, and skillset, with room to progress as impact and tenure grow. Final offer amounts will vary based on candidate profile.

Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity (DIBE) & Accessibility

Our team shows up as their authentic selves, and are united by our mission. We are dedicated to diversity, equity and inclusion. We pride ourselves in building and fostering an environment where our teams feel included, valued, and enabled to do the best work of their careers, wherever they choose to log in from. We believe that different perspectives, skills, backgrounds, and experiences result in higher-performing teams and better innovation. We are committed to equal employment and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

ACR Systems Inc., founded in the mid-1980s in Surrey, BC, is a global leader in data logging solutions, with over one million systems sold worldwide across highly regulated industrial markets. ACR Systems Inc. is recognized for the proven performance, reliability, and durability of its products, tailored to varied needs, locations, and conditions. Day-to-day responsibilities include guiding finance and accounting teams, partnering with executive leadership on business decisions, evaluating investments and capital projects, and providing clear financial insights to support growth and profitability.
